note: Applied Economics (calculations verified), scenario-based Government, applied Commerce (calculations verified).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Ngozi has ₦2,000 and can buy either a textbook or a pair of sandals, each costing ₦2,000. She buys the textbook. Her opportunity cost is
questions.B: both the textbook and the sandals
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone — the sandals she could not buy, not the money itself.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A student lists her wants in order: (1) JAMB form, (2) textbooks, (3) a new phone, (4) shoes. With money for only two items she buys the form and the textbooks. Her list illustrates
questions.explanation: A scale of preference ranks wants in order of importance so that the most pressing ones are satisfied first with limited resources.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following is a positive economic statement?
questions.B: Taxes on the rich ought to be higher
questions.D: An increase in the price of petrol raises transport fares
questions.explanation: A positive statement describes what is and can be tested against facts; statements with 'should', 'ought' or 'deserve' are normative (value judgements).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a country the state owns the major means of production and a central planning body decides what to produce, how to produce it and for whom. This is
questions.explanation: State ownership plus central planning are the defining features of a command (planned/socialist) economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A carpenter buys planks, makes chairs and sells them to a furniture shop, which sells them to customers. The carpenter's activity is an example of
questions.explanation: Turning raw materials (planks) into finished goods (chairs) is manufacturing — secondary production. Extraction is primary; selling and services are tertiary.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Mrs Bello used her savings, hired two tailors, rented a shop and bore the risk of opening a fashion business. The factor of production she herself supplies is
questions.explanation: Organising the other factors and bearing the risk of the business is the role of the entrepreneur.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a Nnewi shoe factory one worker cuts the leather, another stitches it and a third fixes the soles. A likely disadvantage of this arrangement is
questions.A: a fall in the total output of the factory
questions.B: reduced scope for the use of machinery
questions.C: a rise in the average cost of each pair of shoes
questions.D: monotony and loss of all-round craftsmanship
questions.explanation: Division of labour raises output and lowers unit cost, but repeating one small task is boring and workers no longer learn the whole craft.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The price of a brand of noodles stayed the same, yet its sales in Lagos fell sharply after a rival brand cut its price. This is a change in
questions.explanation: A change caused by something other than the good's own price (here, the price of a substitute) shifts the whole demand curve — a change in demand.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: After a good rainy season, tomato farmers brought far more tomatoes to Mile 12 market at every price. On a diagram this is shown as
questions.A: a movement along the supply curve
questions.B: a movement along the demand curve
questions.C: a leftward shift of the supply curve
questions.D: a rightward shift of the supply curve
questions.explanation: More supplied at every price means the supply curve shifts to the right; a movement along the curve happens only when the good's own price changes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a market, demand is Qd = 100 − 2P and supply is Qs = 20 + 2P. The equilibrium price is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium Qd = Qs: 100 − 2P = 20 + 2P ⇒ 80 = 4P ⇒ P = ₦20.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: If demand is Qd = 100 − 2P and supply is Qs = 20 + 2P, the equilibrium quantity is
questions.explanation: Equilibrium price is ₦20 (100 − 2P = 20 + 2P). Substituting: Q = 100 − 2(20) = 60 units.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The government fixes the price of a bag of rice below the equilibrium price. The likely result is
questions.B: an increase in the supply of rice
questions.C: a fall in the demand for rice
questions.D: a shortage of rice and black-marketing
questions.explanation: At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied; the shortage encourages hoarding and black-market sales above the official price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: When the price of a good rose from ₦50 to ₦60, the quantity demanded fell from 200 to 150 units. Using the original values, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: % change in quantity = 50/200 = 25%; % change in price = 10/50 = 20%; elasticity = 25/20 = 1.25 (elastic).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The demand for a product is price inelastic. If the seller raises the price, total revenue will
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand the percentage fall in quantity is smaller than the percentage rise in price, so total revenue (price × quantity) increases.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A 10% rise in the price of garri led to a 5% rise in the quantity of rice demanded. The cross elasticity of demand between rice and garri is ______ and the two goods are ______.
questions.explanation: Cross elasticity = 5%/10% = +0.5. A positive value means the goods are substitutes: dearer garri pushes consumers towards rice.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: When a consumer's monthly income rose from ₦40,000 to ₦50,000, his purchase of eggs rose from 20 to 30 crates. The income elasticity of demand for eggs is
questions.explanation: % change in quantity = 10/20 = 50%; % change in income = 10,000/40,000 = 25%; income elasticity = 50/25 = 2 (a normal, income-elastic good).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A thirsty student gains 10 utils from the first sachet of water, 7 from the second, 4 from the third and 1 from the fourth. The total utility from three sachets is
questions.explanation: Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities: 10 + 7 + 4 = 21 utils.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A thirsty student gains 10 utils from the first sachet of water, 7 from the second, 4 from the third and 1 from the fourth. The falling satisfaction from each extra sachet illustrates the law of
questions.explanation: As more units of a good are consumed, the extra satisfaction from each additional unit falls — the law of diminishing marginal utility.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A farmer keeps adding labourers to a fixed plot of land. After the fifth labourer, each extra worker adds less to total output than the one before. This illustrates
questions.explanation: When more of a variable factor (labour) is added to a fixed factor (land), marginal product eventually falls — the law of diminishing returns.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A bakery's fixed cost is ₦20,000 per day. When it produces 100 loaves its total cost is ₦45,000. The average variable cost per loaf is

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A firm's total cost rises from ₦120,000 to ₦132,000 when output increases from 40 to 44 units. The marginal cost per unit is
questions.explanation: Marginal cost = change in total cost ÷ change in output = 12,000/4 = ₦3,000.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A trader sells 500 mangoes at ₦80 each. Her total cost was ₦30,000. Her profit is

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A firm in a perfectly competitive market sells at ₦50 per unit. Its marginal revenue is
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm is a price taker: each extra unit sells at the market price, so marginal revenue = average revenue = price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Only one company supplies electricity to a whole city and there is no close substitute. This market structure is
questions.explanation: A single seller of a product with no close substitute is a monopoly.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Nigeria's mobile telephone industry is dominated by four large firms whose pricing decisions affect one another. This is an example of
questions.explanation: A few large, interdependent firms dominating a market is an oligopoly.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a closed economy with no government sector, consumption is ₦300 billion and investment is ₦100 billion. National income is
questions.explanation: With no government or foreign trade, Y = C + I = 300 + 100 = ₦400 billion.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country's GDP is ₦50 trillion, net factor income from abroad is −₦2 trillion and depreciation is ₦3 trillion. Its net national product (NNP) is
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 50 − 2 = 48; NNP = GNP − depreciation = 48 − 3 = ₦45 trillion.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country's nominal GDP is ₦60 trillion and its GDP deflator is 120. Real GDP is
questions.explanation: Real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ (deflator/100) = 60 ÷ 1.2 = ₦50 trillion.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A tailor buys cloth for ₦5,000 and sells the finished dress for ₦12,000. The value added by the tailor is
questions.explanation: Value added = value of output − cost of intermediate inputs = 12,000 − 5,000 = ₦7,000.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Counting both the value of flour sold to a bakery and the full value of the bread made from it when computing national income leads to
questions.explanation: The flour's value is already included in the price of the bread; adding it again counts it twice — double counting, avoided by using value added or final goods only.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A farmer in Zamfara wants to exchange his millet for a goat, but the goat owner wants yams instead. This problem of barter is called the lack of
questions.explanation: Barter works only when each party wants exactly what the other offers — a double coincidence of wants — which money removes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Bala keeps part of his salary in a bank to pay school fees in January. Money here is serving as a
questions.explanation: Holding money to spend later is using it as a store of value.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A basket of goods that cost ₦20,000 in January cost ₦25,000 in December of the same year. The rate of inflation for the year is

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A sharp rise in the price of diesel increased transport and production costs, and the prices of most goods rose. This type of inflation is
questions.explanation: When rising costs of inputs push producers to raise prices, the result is cost-push inflation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: During a period of rapid inflation, the group most likely to gain is
questions.A: people who borrowed at a fixed interest rate
questions.B: pensioners living on fixed monthly incomes
questions.C: people who keep their savings in cash at home
questions.D: workers whose salaries are fixed by contract
questions.explanation: Borrowers repay in money that is worth less than what they borrowed; fixed-income earners and savers lose purchasing power.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A persistent fall in the general price level accompanied by falling output and rising unemployment is
questions.explanation: Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level, usually with falling output and jobs; stagflation is stagnation WITH rising prices.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A Nigerian graduate who is willing and able to work cannot find a job because the skills employers want differ from his training. He is experiencing
questions.explanation: A mismatch between workers' skills and the jobs available is structural unemployment.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A labour force of 60 million contains 8 million people who are willing and able to work but have no jobs. The unemployment rate is approximately
questions.explanation: Unemployment rate = unemployed ÷ labour force × 100 = 8/60 × 100 ≈ 13.3%.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country has a population of 200 million and a land area of 1,000,000 km². Its population density is
questions.explanation: Population density = population ÷ land area = 200,000,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = 200 persons per km².

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country's birth rate is 40 per 1,000 and its death rate is 12 per 1,000. Ignoring migration, its natural rate of population growth is
questions.explanation: Natural increase = birth rate − death rate = 28 per 1,000 = 2.8% per year.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country's population is made up largely of people under 15 years of age. One likely consequence is
questions.explanation: Children depend on the working population; a youthful population means many dependants per worker.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Mr Okon earns ₦2,000,000 a year and pays ₦200,000 in income tax; Mrs Ade earns ₦5,000,000 and pays ₦750,000. This tax system is
questions.explanation: Mr Okon pays 10% and Mrs Ade pays 15%: the rate rises with income, which is a progressive tax.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The value added tax (VAT) charged on goods bought in a supermarket is an example of
questions.explanation: VAT is levied on goods and services and passed on to the consumer in the price — an indirect tax.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a year the federal government's revenue was ₦10 trillion while its expenditure was ₦13 trillion. The budget is
questions.explanation: Expenditure exceeds revenue by 13 − 10 = ₦3 trillion, so the budget is in deficit.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: With one unit of resources Country A can produce 10 bags of rice or 5 bales of cotton, while Country B can produce 4 bags of rice or 4 bales of cotton. According to comparative advantage, Country A should specialise in
questions.explanation: A gives up ½ bale of cotton per bag of rice; B gives up 1 bale. A's opportunity cost of rice is lower, so A specialises in rice and B in cotton.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: In a year Nigeria's visible exports were $60 billion and its visible imports $40 billion. Its balance of trade is
questions.explanation: Balance of trade = visible exports − visible imports = 60 − 40 = a $20 billion surplus.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Which of the following transactions is recorded in the invisible account of Nigeria's balance of payments?
questions.A: the export of crude oil to India
questions.B: the import of parboiled rice from Thailand
questions.C: payment to foreign airlines for flights
questions.D: the export of cocoa beans to Europe
questions.explanation: Invisible items are services such as transport, tourism, insurance and banking; goods (oil, rice, cocoa) are visible items.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: The exchange rate changes from ₦1,500 = $1 to ₦1,600 = $1. This means the naira has
questions.explanation: More naira are now needed to buy one dollar, so the naira has lost value — it has depreciated.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A Nigerian importer buys goods worth $2,000 when the exchange rate is ₦1,500 to $1. The naira cost of the goods is

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A government buys surplus cocoa when the world price falls and releases it when the price rises, in order to keep farmers' incomes stable. This policy is
questions.explanation: Buying in gluts and selling in shortages to stabilise price and income is a buffer stock scheme.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A country sets up factories to produce locally the goods it used to import. It is pursuing
questions.explanation: Replacing imports with home-produced goods is the import-substitution strategy of industrialisation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: Country X's GDP grew by 5% last year, yet poverty, illiteracy and infant mortality remained unchanged. Country X experienced
questions.explanation: Growth is a rise in output; development requires improvement in welfare (health, education, poverty). Output rose but welfare did not.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.q: A government sets out targets for output, employment and infrastructure to be achieved over the next five years. This document is
questions.explanation: A medium-term statement of economic targets and the means of achieving them is a development plan; a budget covers one year's revenue and expenditure.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A farmer in Benue grows yams; a lorry driver transports them to Lagos, a wholesaler stores them and a retailer sells them to consumers. All the activities apart from growing the yams fall under
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade and the aids to trade (transport, warehousing, banking, insurance, advertising, communication); growing the yams is production (industry).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A lawyer, a teacher and a doctor render services directly to people. Their occupations are classified as
questions.explanation: Personal services rendered directly to individuals are direct services (tertiary occupations).

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Fishing, mining and lumbering are examples of
questions.explanation: Extractive industries take natural resources directly from land or sea.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A student argues that a lorry driver who carries tomatoes from Jos to Port Harcourt is not a producer because he makes nothing. This is wrong because
questions.A: driving long distances is hard physical work
questions.B: tomatoes would rot if they were not moved quickly
questions.C: the driver is paid wages for the journey
questions.D: the driver adds place utility to the tomatoes
questions.explanation: Production is the creation of utility; transport adds place utility, just as warehousing adds time utility.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The machines, buildings and delivery vans a firm uses to produce goods are examples of
questions.explanation: Capital consists of man-made goods used in further production.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A Nigerian company buys cocoa from farmers in Ondo and sells it to a chocolate maker in Belgium. This transaction is
questions.explanation: Selling goods produced at home to buyers abroad is export trade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Goods are imported into Nigeria and later re-exported to Niger Republic without being processed. This is
questions.explanation: Entrepôt trade is the importation of goods for re-export.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A document issued by a shipping company acknowledging receipt of goods on board and serving as a document of title to them is
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is a receipt, a contract of carriage and a document of title; the holder can claim the goods.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and its visible imports is its
questions.explanation: The balance of trade covers goods only; the balance of payments also includes services and capital flows.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader buys goods on credit. The document the seller sends at the end of the month showing all the transactions and the balance owing is
questions.explanation: A statement of account summarises invoices, payments and returns for the period and shows the amount outstanding.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A buyer returned damaged goods to the seller. The document the seller issues to reduce the amount the buyer owes is
questions.explanation: A credit note (usually printed in red) reduces the buyer's debt; a debit note increases it.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An electronics shop offers 5% off for payment within 7 days. A customer with a ₦120,000 invoice pays on the third day. He pays

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader's opening stock was ₦200,000, purchases for the year ₦800,000 and closing stock ₦300,000. The cost of goods sold is
questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases − closing stock = 200,000 + 800,000 − 300,000 = ₦700,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A wholesaler buys goods with a list price of ₦500,000 at a trade discount of 20%. He pays
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 20% of 500,000 = ₦100,000; amount payable = ₦400,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A manufacturer produces a million sachets of detergent daily, while each shop buys only a few cartons. The wholesaler helps the manufacturer chiefly by
questions.A: advertising the detergent on national television
questions.C: fixing the price at which retailers must sell
questions.D: buying in bulk and breaking bulk for retailers
questions.explanation: The wholesaler buys in large quantities, stores the goods and sells in smaller lots to retailers, relieving the producer of storage and small orders.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A shop in Lagos sells only children's clothing and toys, with trained staff who advise customers. This retailer is
questions.explanation: A shop that deals in one line of goods and offers expert service is a specialist shop.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A retailer bought a phone for ₦80,000 and sold it for ₦100,000. The mark-up as a percentage of cost price is
questions.explanation: Mark-up = profit ÷ cost × 100 = 20,000/80,000 × 100 = 25%. (Margin on selling price would be 20%.)

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Under a hire purchase agreement, ownership of the goods passes to the buyer
questions.C: on payment of the final instalment
questions.explanation: In hire purchase the buyer hires the goods and becomes owner only after the last instalment; under a credit sale ownership passes at once.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A shop's cost of goods sold for the year was ₦1,800,000 and its average stock at cost was ₦300,000. The rate of stock turnover is
questions.explanation: Rate of turnover = cost of goods sold ÷ average stock = 1,800,000/300,000 = 6 times a year.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A bakery sells bread directly to consumers from its own shop. Its channel of distribution is
questions.explanation: Selling straight to the final consumer with no middleman is the shortest (direct) channel.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A Kano trader wants to send 40 tonnes of cement to Lagos as cheaply as possible and is not in a hurry. The most suitable means of transport is
questions.explanation: Rail carries heavy, bulky goods over long distances cheaply, though it is slower and less flexible than road.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Fresh flowers grown in Jos are needed in London within 24 hours. The most suitable means of transport is
questions.explanation: Air transport is the fastest and is ideal for perishable, high-value goods despite its cost.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company wants to send an exact copy of a signed contract to a partner abroad within minutes. The most suitable means is
questions.A: an e-mail with the scanned document attached
questions.B: a telephone call to read out the contract
questions.C: a telegram summarising the main terms
questions.D: a photocopy sent by surface mail
questions.explanation: E-mail delivers documents instantly and an attachment reproduces the signed page exactly.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Imported goods on which customs duty has not yet been paid are kept in
questions.explanation: Bonded warehouses hold dutiable goods under customs control until duty is paid or the goods are re-exported.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A tomato wholesaler keeps stock in cold rooms and releases it gradually through the year. Warehousing here helps to
questions.A: raise prices by creating artificial scarcity
questions.B: improve the quality of the tomatoes
questions.C: stabilise prices by evening out supply
questions.D: avoid paying tax on unsold stock
questions.explanation: Storing goods from times of plenty to times of scarcity smooths supply and keeps prices steadier.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A building worth ₦20 million was insured for ₦10 million. Fire caused damage of ₦4 million. Under the average clause the insurer pays
questions.explanation: Under-insurance: payment = loss × (sum insured ÷ value) = 4 × 10/20 = ₦2 million.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: After an accident Mr Eze received from his insurer exactly the cost of repairing his car, and no more. The principle applied is
questions.explanation: Indemnity restores the insured to his position before the loss; he must not profit from insurance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A man insured his neighbour's house, hoping to collect money if it burnt down. His claim would fail because he lacks
questions.explanation: One can insure only something whose loss would cause one financial loss — insurable interest.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: When applying for life assurance, Mrs Ojo concealed the fact that she had a heart condition. The insurer can repudiate a claim because she breached the principle of
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) requires the proposer to disclose all material facts.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader pays ₦50,000 a year to an insurer to cover his shop against fire. The ₦50,000 is the
questions.explanation: The premium is the consideration paid for insurance cover; the policy is the contract document.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A trader wants a cheque that cannot be cashed over the counter but must be paid into a bank account. He should
questions.explanation: Two parallel lines across the face of a cheque (crossing) mean it can only be paid through a bank account, which is safer.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A customer's cheque was returned by the bank marked 'refer to drawer'. The most likely reason is that
questions.explanation: 'Refer to drawer' (R/D) usually means there is not enough money in the drawer's account to honour the cheque.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Mrs Ade deposited ₦200,000 in a savings account paying 5% simple interest per annum. After 2 years she earns interest of
questions.explanation: Simple interest = principal × rate × time = 200,000 × 0.05 × 2 = ₦20,000.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The bank that issues the naira, supervises other banks and acts as banker to the federal government is the
questions.explanation: These are the functions of a central bank; in Nigeria it is the CBN.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Chidi bought 1,000 shares of a company at ₦25 each and received a dividend of ₦2 per share. His dividend yield is
questions.explanation: Dividend yield = dividend per share ÷ price per share × 100 = 2/25 × 100 = 8%.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An investor buys shares expecting their price to rise so that he can sell them at a profit. He is called
questions.explanation: A bull buys expecting prices to rise; a bear sells expecting a fall; a stag buys new issues to resell quickly.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Two friends pool ₦5 million, run a restaurant together and share the profits, but each is personally liable for all the debts of the business. Their business is
questions.explanation: Joint ownership by two to twenty persons sharing profits, with unlimited liability, is an ordinary partnership.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A cement company invites the general public to buy its shares, which are traded on the Nigerian Exchange. It is
questions.explanation: Only a public limited company (Plc) may offer its shares to the public and have them quoted on the stock exchange.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A shareholder of a limited company loses only the amount he invested when the company fails. This is because of
questions.explanation: Limited liability restricts a member's loss to the amount unpaid on his shares; his personal property is safe.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company wishing to raise long-term capital without giving up any ownership can issue
questions.explanation: Debentures are loans to the company; holders are creditors, not owners, and receive fixed interest.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A supplier delivers ₦2 million worth of goods to a retailer, to be paid for in 60 days. The retailer is financing his stock through
questions.explanation: Buying goods now and paying later is trade credit — a short-term source of finance.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The manager of a firm divides the work among departments and assigns authority and responsibility to each. This function of management is
questions.explanation: Organising is arranging people, tasks and authority so that plans can be carried out.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company reduced the price of its soap, redesigned the packaging, advertised on radio and made the soap available in rural markets. The four elements it adjusted are the
questions.explanation: Product, price, promotion and place are the 4Ps of the marketing mix.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A company gives out free samples of a new toothpaste in a market and offers 'buy two, get one free'. This is
questions.explanation: Short-term incentives such as free samples, coupons and bonus packs are sales promotion.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: An advertisement simply announces that a new brand of malt drink is now available, stating its price and where to buy it. This type of advertising is
questions.explanation: Informative advertising gives facts about a product without attempting to compare or persuade.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: A customer bought a blender that stopped working after two days and the seller refused to replace it. The federal agency to which she should complain is the
questions.A: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
questions.B: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
questions.explanation: The FCCPC handles consumer complaints and enforces consumer rights in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: Manufacturers in Nigeria have come together in the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) mainly to
questions.A: fix the retail prices of manufactured goods
questions.B: protect and promote the common interests of members
questions.C: collect company taxes on behalf of government
questions.D: take over the functions of the chambers of commerce
questions.explanation: Trade associations speak for their members, lobby government and provide information and standards.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The government bans the importation of rice to protect local farmers. This trade policy instrument is
questions.explanation: A total ban on the import of a product is an embargo; a quota limits the quantity; a tariff is a tax.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.q: The government imposes a 20% duty on imported cars. This is
questions.explanation: A tax on imported goods is a tariff (customs duty).

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria rejected a foreign country's attempt to dictate its trade laws, insisting that only its own government can make laws for Nigerians. This illustrates
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the supreme power of a state to make and enforce laws within its territory free from external control.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A traffic warden directs vehicles and drivers obey because the law empowers him to do so. The warden is exercising
questions.explanation: Authority is the right to command that comes from an office recognised by law; power is the mere ability to compel.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: After a keenly contested election, citizens widely accept the new government's right to rule. The government is said to enjoy
questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the popular acceptance of a government's right to govern.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In Country X the head of state inherited the throne, but real power is exercised by an elected parliament and prime minister. Country X is
questions.explanation: A hereditary monarch who reigns but does not rule, with power in elected institutions, is a constitutional monarchy (e.g. the United Kingdom).

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A small group of wealthy families controls all the important offices of government in a country. This form of government is
questions.explanation: Oligarchy is rule by a small privileged group.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The National Assembly passes a bill, the President assents to it, and later the Supreme Court declares a section of it unconstitutional. The court is exercising
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of the courts to declare laws or actions of the other arms void where they conflict with the constitution.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Senate refuses to confirm a ministerial nominee sent by the President. This is an example of
questions.explanation: One arm of government restraining another is checks and balances; separation of powers merely assigns different functions to different arms.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The National Assembly gives a ministry power to make detailed regulations under an Act. Those regulations are an example of
questions.explanation: Laws made by a body other than the legislature under powers granted by the legislature are delegated (subsidiary) legislation.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In a country the head of government is chosen from the majority party in parliament and can be removed by a vote of no confidence. This is a
questions.explanation: Fusion of the executive and the legislature, with the cabinet responsible to parliament, defines the parliamentary (cabinet) system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In Nigeria's Fourth Republic the President is both head of state and head of government and is elected separately from the legislature. This is a feature of the
questions.explanation: A separately elected chief executive who combines both roles is the hallmark of the presidential system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In Country Y the central government can create or abolish regional governments at will, and the regions derive all their powers from the centre. Country Y operates
questions.explanation: In a unitary state all power belongs to the centre, which may delegate to (and withdraw from) lower units as it wishes.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's constitution shares law-making powers between the federal and state governments through the exclusive, concurrent and residual lists. This arrangement is called
questions.explanation: Constitutional division of powers between a central government and component units, each supreme in its own sphere, is federalism.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A government takes over the major industries, abolishes private ownership of large businesses and plans the economy centrally in the name of equality. This ideology is
questions.explanation: Public ownership of the means of production and central planning in pursuit of equality are socialist principles.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In Country Z the constitution can be amended by a simple majority in parliament, in the same way as an ordinary law. Its constitution is
questions.explanation: A constitution amended by the ordinary law-making procedure is flexible; one needing a special procedure is rigid.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The 1999 Constitution of Nigeria can be altered only with the approval of two-thirds of each house of the National Assembly and of the Houses of Assembly of at least two-thirds of the states. This shows that the constitution is
questions.explanation: A special, difficult amendment procedure makes a constitution rigid.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A former state governor was arrested and tried for corruption after leaving office, just like any other citizen. This illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Equality before the law — nobody is above the law — is a central element of the rule of law.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A newspaper publishes a story sharply critical of the President and is not shut down. This best illustrates
questions.explanation: Freedom of the press and of expression are basic features of a democratic government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A bill has passed its first and second readings in the House of Representatives. The next stage is the
questions.explanation: The order is: first reading, second reading (debate on principles), committee stage (detailed examination), report stage, third reading, then the other chamber and assent.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The President refuses to sign a bill passed by the National Assembly. Under the 1999 Constitution the bill can still become law if
questions.A: the Senate President signs it on the President's behalf
questions.B: each house passes it again by a two-thirds majority
questions.C: the Supreme Court declares it constitutional
questions.D: the Council of State approves it by a simple majority
questions.explanation: Section 58 provides that if assent is withheld, the National Assembly may pass the bill again by two-thirds majority and it becomes law without assent.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Mr Kwame, a Ghanaian, has lived in Nigeria for 20 years, is of good character and applies to become a Nigerian citizen. If granted, he becomes a citizen by
questions.explanation: A foreigner who acquires citizenship after long residence and meeting the legal conditions is naturalised.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Which of the following is a duty of a Nigerian citizen rather than a right?
questions.explanation: Rights are what the citizen is entitled to; paying taxes, obeying the law and defending the country are duties.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: To be declared winner of a Nigerian presidential election, a candidate must have the highest number of votes and at least
questions.A: one-quarter of the votes cast in each of at least two-thirds of the states and the FCT
questions.B: one-half of the votes cast in each of the thirty-six states
questions.C: two-thirds of the votes cast in at least half of the states
questions.D: the votes of a majority of all registered voters in the federation
questions.explanation: Section 134 of the 1999 Constitution requires a spread of not less than 25% of the votes in at least two-thirds of the states and the Federal Capital Territory.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A system in which parties win seats in proportion to their share of the total votes cast is
questions.explanation: Proportional representation allocates seats according to each party's percentage of votes.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In a constituency election Candidate A scored 40%, B 35% and C 25% of the votes, and A was declared the winner. The electoral system used is
questions.explanation: A won without more than half of the votes; a plurality is enough under the simple majority system.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The body responsible for conducting federal and state elections in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: INEC organises and supervises federal and state elections; state electoral commissions handle local government elections.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A country has many registered parties, but only two of them have a realistic chance of forming the government. Its party system is best described as
questions.explanation: A two-party system exists where two major parties dominate and alternate in power, even if minor parties exist.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The main difference between a political party and a pressure group is that a political party
questions.B: aims to win elections and control the government
questions.explanation: Both influence policy, but only a party contests elections in order to take over government.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigeria Labour Congress threatens a nationwide strike to force the government to raise the minimum wage. The NLC is acting as
questions.explanation: A pressure group seeks to influence government decisions in its members' interest without seeking to govern.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigerian Medical Association campaigns for better pay and working conditions for doctors. It is best classified as
questions.explanation: Sectional or professional groups defend the economic interests of their own members; promotional groups pursue a cause for society at large.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A radio phone-in programme gathers strong public objections to a new levy, and the government later withdraws it. This shows the role of
questions.explanation: Public opinion — the views of the people on an issue — can influence and restrain government policy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A permanent secretary who served under one ruling party continues in office when a different party wins the election. This illustrates the civil-service principle of
questions.explanation: Career civil servants remain in office when governments change — permanence. Neutrality refers to not taking political sides.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A minister publicly takes responsibility for an error made by officials in her ministry, whose names are never mentioned. This illustrates the civil-service principle of
questions.explanation: Civil servants act in the minister's name and are not publicly identified — anonymity; the minister answers for the ministry.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the pre-colonial Igbo political system, village decisions were taken at the general assembly of adult males and by the council of elders, with no king. The system was
questions.explanation: Acephalous means 'without a head': authority was shared among assemblies, elders, age grades and title societies rather than held by a king.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: In the Old Oyo Empire the Oyo Mesi could compel an unpopular Alaafin to commit suicide by presenting him with an empty calabash. This shows that the system had
questions.B: checks and balances on the Alaafin
questions.explanation: The Oyo Mesi (and the Ogboni) limited the Alaafin's power — a traditional system of checks and balances.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The British governed Northern Nigeria through the emirs and their existing institutions. This system was called
questions.explanation: Indirect rule used traditional rulers as agents of colonial administration.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Indirect rule was least successful in Eastern Nigeria mainly because
questions.A: the people had rejected Christianity and Western education
questions.B: the area had no centralised traditional rulers, so warrant chiefs were imposed
questions.C: the British had too few soldiers stationed in the region
questions.D: the region was too large and thickly populated to administer
questions.explanation: The Igbo system was acephalous; the artificial warrant chiefs lacked legitimacy, leading to resentment and the 1929 Aba Women's Riot.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A major effect of the Second World War on Nigerian nationalism was that
questions.A: it brought nationalist agitation to an end for a decade
questions.B: returning soldiers and wartime experiences intensified demands for self-government
questions.C: Nigeria was granted independence immediately the war ended
questions.D: the British granted universal adult suffrage to all Nigerians
questions.explanation: Ex-servicemen who had fought for freedom abroad, the Atlantic Charter and economic hardship all strengthened the demand for self-rule after 1945.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Nigerian constitution that first established a truly federal system of government was the
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution made the regions autonomous with their own powers — the beginning of federalism; Richards only introduced regionalism.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is remembered mainly for
questions.explanation: It allowed, for the first time, the election of four Africans (three for Lagos, one for Calabar) into the Legislative Council.

questions.subject: Government
questions.topic: Political Parties and the First Republic
questions.q: In the First Republic the NPC, NCNC and AG drew their main support respectively from the
questions.explanation: The Northern People's Congress was based in the North, the NCNC in the East and the Action Group in the West — parties were largely regional.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The first military coup in Nigeria took place in
questions.explanation: The coup of 15 January 1966 ended the First Republic; the counter-coup followed in July 1966.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: A common feature of military regimes in Nigeria was that they governed by
questions.explanation: Military governments suspended parts of the constitution and legislated by decree (federal) and edicts (state).

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The Second Republic (1979–1983) differed from the First Republic mainly in that it operated
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution replaced the Westminster parliamentary model with an American-style executive presidency.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The presidential election of 12 June 1993, widely believed to have been won by M.K.O. Abiola, was
questions.A: upheld by the Supreme Court of Nigeria
questions.B: annulled by the Babangida military government
questions.C: won by Bashir Tofa of the NRC
questions.D: boycotted by voters in most states
questions.explanation: The annulment of the June 12 election ended the transition to the Third Republic.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's Fourth Republic began on
questions.explanation: Civilian rule returned on 29 May 1999 with the inauguration of President Olusegun Obasanjo under the 1999 Constitution.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Matters such as defence, currency and foreign affairs, on which only the National Assembly may legislate, are on the
questions.explanation: The exclusive list is reserved for the federal government; both tiers may legislate on the concurrent list; residual matters belong to the states.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The number of local government areas listed in the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The First Schedule of the 1999 Constitution lists 774 local government areas.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The government sold its majority shares in a state-owned electricity company to private investors. This is
questions.explanation: Transferring ownership of public enterprises to private hands is privatisation; nationalisation is the reverse.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's foreign policy has consistently given priority to African affairs, for example its support for liberation movements in Southern Africa. This principle is known as
questions.B: Africa as the centrepiece of foreign policy
questions.explanation: Successive governments have made Africa the centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: Nigeria's leading role in the ECOMOG peacekeeping operations in Liberia and Sierra Leone in the 1990s demonstrates its commitment to
questions.A: regional peace and security in West Africa
questions.explanation: Nigeria provided most of the troops and funding for ECOMOG to restore peace in the sub-region.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: The organ of the United Nations in which five permanent members have the power of veto is the
questions.explanation: The USA, Russia, China, the UK and France are permanent members of the Security Council and can veto substantive resolutions.

questions.subject: Government
questions.q: ECOWAS was established by the Treaty of Lagos in 1975 mainly to
questions.A: create a common army for West Africa
questions.B: promote economic integration among West African states
questions.D: replace the Organisation of African Unity
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States was formed to promote trade, co-operation and economic integration in the sub-region.
